msContents.summary:
[p][b]Contents[/b][/p]
[p]1. f. 2r Illustration of a vein man, with explanatory text[/p]
[p]2. f. 2v Astrological chart[/p]
[p]3. ff. 3r-4r Commentary on the five opening lines of the [i]Carmina de urinis[/i] of Gilles de Corbeil[/p]
The [i]Carmina de urinis[/i], written by Gilles de Corbeil in the late twelfth-century, was one of the key components of the medieval [i]Articella[/i], the corpus of texts that medical students were expected to learn and know. On Gilles's life and works, see Mireille Ausécache, 'Gilles de Corbeil, ou le médecin pédagogue au tournant des XIIe et XIIIe siècles', [i]Early Science and Medicine[/i] 3:3 (1998), pp. 187-214.[/p]
[p]Incipit: 'Dictur urina quum sit renibus una....'[/p]
[p]Explicit: '…ad mediam regionem urine uel suppremam'.[/p]
[p]4. f. 4r-v Recipe for ulcers[/p]
[p]Incipit: 'Pocio probata per magistrum galterum de M contra uulcera noua et uetera...'[/p]
[p]Explicit: '...et in lacte dulci coquitur et tepida explicetur. Hoc emplastrum optimum esse probatur.'[/p]
[p]5. ff. 5r-12v Johannes de Sancto Paulo, [i]Flores dietarum[/i][/p]
[p]Incipit: 'Corpus nostrum ex iiii constat humoribus...'[/p]
[p]Explicit: '…qui tibi donet gratiam sue misericordie et ueniam peccatorum qui sit benedictus in secula seculorum amen'.[/p]
[p]6. ff. 13r-34 Matthaeus Platearius, [i]Circa instans[/i][/p]
[p]Incipit: 'Circa instans negocium in simplicibus medicinis...'[/p]
[p]Explicit: '...iam lasso pollice sistat opus. Explicit liber platearii de singulari et simplici medicina.'[/p]
[p]On Matthaeus Platearius's [i]Circa instans[/i] see Frank J. Anderson, [i]An Illustrated History of the Herbals[/i] (New York: Columbia University Press, 1997), pp. 45-50; and Minta Collins, [i]Medieval Herbals: The Illustrative Traditions[/i] (London: The British Library, 2000), pp. 239, 243, 285-286, 298, 307-308.[/p]
[p]7. f. 34r-v List of diseases[/p]
[p]Begins: 'De dolore capitis'[/p]
[p]Ends :'De duricie splenis'.[/p]
[p]8. f. 34v Medical receipts[/p]
[p]9. ff. 35r-56 [i]Glossulae quatuor magistrorum[/i] edited by Guido Aretinus, abbreviated[/p]
[p]Incipit: 'Sicut dicit constantinus humores temperamentum exeuntes faciunt causam morbi...'[/p]
[p]Explicit (f. 55r): '...quoniam comedere semel nocet eis sicut dict auicenna. Explicit'. [Followed by a further portion of the work, which had been omitted by the scribe at fol. 54v, line 52: it is marked with a sign -o- at beginning and end].
[p]8. ff. 56r-65r Nicholas of Salerno, [i]Antidotarium[/i][/p]
[p]Incipit: 'Ego nicolaus rogatus a quibusdam in practica medicina studere uolentibus...'[/p]
[p]Explicit: '...copiam nummorum et amicorum plenitudine glorientur'.[/p]
[p]9. ff. 65r-66v Serapion Junior, [i]Libri aggregationum[/i], incomplete[/p]
[p]Incipit: 'Postquam uidi librum dyascoridis et librum G. in medicinis simplicibus... '[/p]
[p]Ends imperfectly: '…immutando. in primum. et immutacio medicine curauit'.[/p]
[p]10. ff. 67r-69r Otho Candidus, [i]Constitutiones[/i], incomplete[/p]
[p]Incipit: 'Incipiunt constitutiones Otonis Quoniam decet domui domini sanctitudo...'[/p]
[p]Ends imperfectly: '...decreuimus fore priuatum'.[/p]
[p]11. ff. 69r-78v Ottobonus, [i]Constitutiones[/i], incomplete[/p]
[p]Incipit: Statuta uenerabilis patris in christo Domini Ottoboni Sancti Adriani diaconi cardinalis Apostolice sedis in Anglia legati pupplicata in generali concilio eiusdem legati in ecclesia Sancti Pauli Londonie. Mense aprilis die lune proxima ante diem Sancti Marci Evangeliste Anno domini MoCCmo sexagesimo octauo. [O]ttobonus apostolice sedis legatus miseracione diuina Sancti Adriani diaconus…'[/p]
[p]Ends imperfectly: '…de excommunicato capiendo denegetur cum regulis [?] contingat inde [?]…'[/p]
[p]12. f. 79r Receipt[/p]
[p]Begins: 'Confectio pulueris sine pauore, gallice sains peur...'[/p]

msItem.title: Compendium of learned medical texts (Miscellanea Medica VI)

objectDesc.supportDesc: 1 volume79 ll. folio. 31 x 21 1/2 cm. On vellum; modern half calf binding over wooden boards in 15th century monastic style. The end of the 'Liber aggregationum' of Serapion Junior-after fol. 66, and the end of the 'Constitutiones' of Ottobonus-after fol. 78, are wanting. Many leaves are stained and worn.
